newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end down ahead of election campaign.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end down ahead of election campaign.

text.p: Jakarta stocks closed slightly down on Friday as active local speculative buying of small stocks prevented a larger fall because of nervousnes ahead of the start of the election campaign on Sunday, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index fell 0.51 points, or 0.08 percent, to close at 652.48 points. Advancers led decliners by 65 to 52 with 71 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was 462 billion rupiah compared with 430 billion rupiah on Thursday.
"Overall sentiment remained firm as you can see that gainers far outnumbered losers and that some big-caps like Timah and Barito were among the gainers," one broker said.
Brokers said falls in big-caps Gudang Garam, Sampoerna and Telkom could be attributed to cautious sentiment on the part of foreign players ahead of the start of the election campaign.
Brokers, however, said most local players saw little possibility of a sharp fall in the index in the coming week and expected to remain active in small stocks.

"Foreign players are likely to stay on the sidelines after the start of the election campaign, and unless there is some trouble, the index is likely to rally after the election," one analyst with a foreign brokerage firm said.
The analyst said the index is likely to reach 750 levels at the end of the year on the back of the country's firm economic fundamentals.
Small property firm Elang Realty rose 175 rupiah to 1,475 rupiah, with some 57 billion shares traded, making it the most active share for the whole week.
There were some rumours in the market that Elang was likely to be lifted to 1,500 rupiah. This issue has prompted players to continue buying Elang despite its recent sharp increases, brokers said.
The second most actively traded counter was another small property firm, Suryamas, which rose 25 rupiah to 700 rupiah on reports of a plan to link up with another firm, brokers said.
